figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3.   Effects of NADP+ on the kinetics of the oxidative half-­reaction of AetF. (A) Kinetics of the reaction of the reduced AetF with oxygen (air-­saturation) in the 
presence or absence of NADP+ monitored by absorbance changes at 360 nm and 450 nm. The reactions were carried out in a 50 mM MOPS pH 8.0 buffer with 
10% v/v glycerol at 25 °C. (B) Spectra of flavin species involved in the reaction of the reduced AetF with an oxygenated solution (100%) of 10% v/v glycerol in a 
50 mM MOPS pH 8.0 buffer in the presence of NADP+ at 25 °C. The data were analyzed using the ReactLab Kinetics program. The starting species of the reaction 
(Spectrum A) is the reduced AetF (RedAetF). The intermediate of the reaction (Spectrum B) is the C4a-­hydroperoxy flavin (FADC4aOOH). The final species (Spectrum 
C) is the oxidized AetF (OxAetF). (C) A reaction scheme describing the requirement of NADP+ for FADC4aOOH stabilization.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4.   Kinetics of the oxidative half-­reaction of AetF in the presence of substrates. (A) Kinetics of absorbance changes at 360 nm and 450 nm of the reaction 
of 20 μM reduced AetF in the presence of 200 μM NADP+ with the oxygenated solution (air-­saturated) containing 200 μM L-­tryptophan, or 20 mM NaBr, or both

kinetic traces of absorption and fluorescence changes of the reaction in the presence of NaBr. (F) Absorption spectra of the reaction in the presence of 20 mM 
NaBr monitored over an extended time scale (up to 4,000 s).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5.   Mechanisms of flavin reactions and tryptophan halogenation catalyzed by AetF. (A) Full catalytic cycle of AetF with the rate constants. The catalytic cycle 
begins with reduction of the oxidized AetF by NADPH to form reduced AetF with NADP+ bound. The complex then reacts with oxygen to form C4a-­hydroperoxy 
FAD (AetF-­C4aOOH). In the absence of both halide ion (X−) and L-­tryptophan (L-­TRP), FADC4aOOH undergoes hydrogen peroxide elimination to form oxidized FAD 
slowly (gray line). In the presence of halide ion, we propose that X− may bind at the initial step or at the step before or after FADC4aOOH formation to form HOX 
and C4a-­hydroxy FAD (AetF-­C4aOH). In the presence of L-­TRP (blue lines), FAD-­oxygen adduct (possibly FADC4aOH) returns to oxidized FAD faster compared to the 
reaction without L-­TRP (red lines). We could not identify the L-­TRP binding step based on the current data. However, due to rapid binding and spacious active 
site, we propose that L-­TRP possibly binds at the initial oxidized AetF before or after FADC4aOOH formation. Finally, the product and NADP+ leave from the active 
sites to reset the AetF for the next catalytic cycle. (B) The simplified proposed catalytic mechanism of AetF.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6.   Analysis of AetF structures. (A) Flavin and NADP+ binding in the AetF:FAD:NADP+ complex (PDB: 8JZ5). (B) Binding of NADP+ in phenylacetone 
monooxygenase:FAD:NADP+ complex (PDB: 2YLR). (C) Tunnel analysis of the AetF:FAD complex (PDB: 8CJD) compared to AetF:FAD:NADP+ complex (PDB: 8JZ5). 
The biological tunnel is represented in blue. (D) Water molecules in AetF:FAD:NADP+ complex (PDB: 8JZ5); gray spheres and a water molecule in AetF:FAD complex 
(PDB: 8CJD); blue sphere. (E) A water molecule located near the C4a position at the re-­side of FAD in L-­ornithine hydroxylase (SidA) structure (PDB: 4B63). (F) 
Tunnel analysis of the AetF:FAD complex (PDB: 8CJD) compared to the AetF:FAD:L-­TRP complex (PDB: 8CJE). The biological tunnel is represented in blue with 
amino acid residues lining the tunnel. The R370 residue is represented in green sticks. The data clearly illustrate that the binding of NADP+ and L-­TRP induces 
changes in tunnel characteristics and the water network surrounding the flavin binding sites, potentially influencing the mechanism of AetF.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 7.   Effects of NADP+ on biocatalysis of AetF. (A) Photobiocatalysis catalyzing bromination of aromatic compounds by AetF. The tested aromatic compounds were 
tryptophan (1a), phenol (2a), and carbazole (3a). (B) The chromatograms of brominated tryptophans with the m/z isotope pattern of dibromo-­L-­tryptophan (Inset) 
after 24 h of the reaction analyzed by Ultra High Performance Liquid Chromatography equipped with a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer (UHPLC-­MS/MS). (C) The 
extracted ion chromatograms (EIC) of brominated phenol (m/z 173.01) with the m/z isotope pattern (Inset) after 25 h of the reaction analyzed by GC-­MS. (D) The EIC of 
brominated carbazole (m/z 246.10) with the m/z isotope pattern (Inset) after 25 h of the reaction analyzed by GC-­MS. (E) Kinetics of absorbance changes at 360 nm and 
450 nm of the reaction of 20 μM reduced AetF in the presence of 200 μM NADP+ with the oxygenated solution (air-­saturated) containing 20 mM NaBr and substrate 
(200 μM phenol or 200 μM carbazole) in 10% v/v glycerol, 50 mM MOPS pH 8.0 buffer at 25 °C.
